text: In the field of psychology. <break time="0.8s" /> There is a concept called intermittent reinforcement. <break time="0.8s" /> That helps us to understand the challenges created by twenty first century technology. <break time="0.8s" /> To illustrate this idea. <break time="0.8s" /> Imagine a mouse in a cage. <break time="0.8s" /> If you drop a food pellet into the cage. <break time="0.8s" /> At the same time every day. <break time="0.8s" /> The mouse eventually begins to look for the pellet. <break time="0.8s" /> Only at the expected time. <break time="0.8s" /> If, however, you distribute the food pellet. <break time="0.8s" /> At random times throughout the day. <break time="0.8s" /> The mouse soon begins to look for the pellet. <break time="0.8s" /> Virtually all the time. <break time="0.8s" /> That is intermittent reinforcement. <break time="0.8s" /> The mouse does not know. <break time="0.8s" /> When the reward will come. <break time="0.8s" /> So it is driven to check frequently. <break time="0.8s" /> Busy people with access to many communication tools. <break time="0.8s" /> Exhibit the same type of drive. <break time="0.8s" /> Email, voicemail, and other forms of communication. <break time="0.8s" /> Bring good news, neutral news, and sometimes bad news. <break time="0.8s" /> And we never know which it will be or when it will come. <break time="0.8s" /> Which creates a strong temptation to check for updates continuously.
